about.headline: 🌌 Sky Map
about.tagline: An interactive astronomy app built to modern scientific standards
about.intro: A 3D interactive sky map that runs directly in your device's browser, simulating the sky above you with high astronomical accuracy across a span of 20,000 years (9999 BCE to 9999 CE). The app combines the latest internationally adopted models (IAU 2006, JPL Horizons) with data from world observatories (ESA: Hipparcos and Gaia DR3) to deliver a complete observing experience: from bright stars above the horizon to the depths of the Milky Way, from the present moment to the deep past and far future — with astronomical calculations of celestial events, instant search, and full support for six languages.
about.engine_body:
Every calculation in the app passes through internationally adopted models — no simplified approximations:

Standard / ModelPurposeSource
IAU 2006 PrecessionEarth's axis precession (~25,772-year cycle) via a continuously updated precession matrixInternational Astronomical Union
IAU 2006 Mean ObliquityEarth's obliquity for the reference ecliptic frame (long-term numerical stability)International Astronomical Union
True Equator & Equinox of DateReference frame at the instant of observation (includes aberration and nutation for the apparent Sun)Modern astronomical standard
JPL HorizonsPlanetary positions across ±9999 years in a compact binary formatNASA — Jet Propulsion Laboratory
VSOP87 + ELP-2000/82Planetary and lunar motion theories inside the computation engineParis Observatory / Chapront
Morrison–StephensonComputing ΔT (difference between Terrestrial Time TT and Universal Time UT) with an ELP-2000/82 correctionAdopted historical model
ICRS / J2000.0Standard reference frame for all stellar cataloguesIAU
Terrestrial Time + Julian DateDisplaying Terrestrial Time (TT) and the astronomical Julian DayAstronomical standard

💡 Why does this matter? Most popular astronomy apps settle for the older IAU 1976 precession model. Here the newer IAU 2006 is used together with the true «of-date» frame, so the results match professional observing software such as Stellarium and SkySafari.

🛠 Star-catalogue accuracy: Gaia DR3 data is stored at the official reference epoch J2016.0 (JD 2457389.0 TCB). Proper-motion propagation runs on the great circle p′ = p·cosθ + t̂·sinθ — the exact model at every declination including the polar regions — honouring the catalogue convention pmra = μα·cosδ with automatic epoch alignment (Δt = years − 16).
about.stars_body:
• 🌟 Bright stars (Hipparcos/HYG) — catalogue of luminous stars with proper motion and true colours, stored in the J2000 frame.
  • 🌌 Gaia DR3 stars (up to 2 million) — the latest release of ESA's Gaia space observatory, with a smart structure:
    • Global layer (GlobalBright): the brightest ~5% of stars load instantly with the app.
    • 72 deep tiles (12 × 30° in RA × 6 × 30° in Dec) stream in according to your viewing direction in batches of no more than ~7ms so the interface never freezes.
  • 🎨 Physical colours — Gaia's BP-RP colour index converted to RGB by stellar temperature (from hot blue O/B to orange-red M).
  • 🏷️ Dynamic labelling — star names appear according to apparent magnitude and the number of stars displayed, adapting to zoom.
  • 🕰️ Live proper motion — stars genuinely move on the map through time! Try jumping to year 3000 or −5000 and watch fast-moving nearby stars drift (Barnard's being the most famous) — with real catalogue rates, the exact great-circle model, and full consistency between the drawn star, its click target and its info panel at all times.
about.bodies_body:
• ☀️ The Sun — high-resolution surface map (8K) and an apparent position in the of-date frame.
  • 🌙 The Moon — ELP-2000/82 theory with realistically computed phases and a detailed surface map.
  • 🪐 All solar-system planets including Pluto — JPL positions across ±9999 years, with a texture map for each planet (up to 8K from Solar System Scope and Wikimedia).
  • 💍 Saturn's rings in 3D with a true orbital tilt.
  • 💫 Realistic solar lighting — planets are shown at their actual phase (lit side toward the Sun), with adjustable ambient light.
about.deepsky_body:
• 🌌 The Milky Way — the true panorama from the European Southern Observatory (ESO).
  • 🔭 110 Messier objects (M1–M110) — nebulae, clusters and galaxies, with toggleable labels and an independent info card (type, magnitude, size, distance, constellation).
  • 🎛️ Independent display controls — enable/hide and label each object family from Settings.
about.constellations_body:
• 🗺️ Official IAU constellation boundaries — the 88 adopted constellations (Delporte 1930) drawn on the equatorial frame with precession rotation.
  • 🏷️ IAU constellation names — shown at each constellation's centre (Arabic/English per language).
  • 🎨 Artistic constellation figures — modern illustrations in the Stellarium style, with adjustable opacity and automatic fade-out when zooming in (FOV < 45°).
  • ➰ Constellation lines — the lines joining a constellation's stars, independently toggleable.
about.grids_body:
Five complete astronomical grids with dynamic numbering that adapts to the zoom level:

GridColourDescription
🔵 Equatorial (of date)BlueThe celestial equator and RA/Dec lines at the moment of observation after precession
🟣 Reference equatorial (J2000)PurpleThe fixed reference equatorial frame
🟡 Ecliptic (of date)GoldThe current ecliptic with ecliptic longitude/latitude lines
🩷 Reference ecliptic (J2000)PinkThe reference ecliptic (mean obliquity of IAU 2006)
🟢 AltazimuthGreenThe horizon with altitude and azimuth lines
  • 🧭 Ten direction marks: N · NE · E · SE · S · SW · W · NW · Zenith · Nadir.
  • 🔢 Grid numbering — coordinate values along the circles, spaced intelligently by zoom.
  • ⭕ Main circle — the reference horizon ring of the celestial dome.
about.zodiac_body:
Zodiac systems:

  • 🌍 Tropical — the Western reference zodiac on the live equinoctial point.
  • 🌌 Sidereal (J2000) — the fixed astronomical zodiac on the reference ecliptic.
  • 🔄 Both — display both systems together for direct visual comparison (cyan/yellow boundaries).

Sidereal longitude references (optional):

  • ✨ Spica-180° (Lahiri) — the official Indian reference.
  • 🌌 Galactic centre — the modern astronomical reference.
  • 🔴 Aldebaran and 🟠 Antares — the two traditional stellar references.
  • ✏️ Custom longitude — enter any longitude in degrees measured from the start of Aries (0°) on the J2000 reference ecliptic, or pick a reference date from which the drift is computed.

Drawing modes: fixed 30° boundaries per sign, or variable per the actual zodiacal year.

Lunar mansions (28 stations): the ancient Arabic system from Al-Sharatan to Al-Rasha — for any object the app computes its current mansion and its percentage within it (shown in the info panel and zodiac section).
about.calc_title: 📅 Astronomical Calculations — 12 Categories of Celestial Events
about.calc_body:
An independent window with events timed to the second, on/off filters per category, an adjustable initial computation span, and on-demand loading of additional months:

CategoryContent
🌙 Lunar phasesNew moon, first quarter, full moon, last quarter — with altazimuth coordinates
☀️ Sun entering signsMoments of entry in both tropical and sidereal systems
🪩 Moon entering signsThe swift Moon crossing signs and mansions
🪐 Planets entering signsAll planets (including Pluto) with retrograde ↺ / direct ↻ motion detection
⭐ SupermoonFull or new moon closer than 365,000 km, with the distance in kilometres
⚪️⚫️ Apogee & perigeeFarthest/nearest points of the Moon from Earth
🌦️ SeasonsThe four equinoxes and solstices
💢 ConjunctionsTwo planets approaching within < 5°
💦 OppositionsAngular separation ≈ 180° between two planets (±5°)
🌙 Lunar nodesAscending ☊ and descending ☋ nodes with crossing direction
☀️🌑 Solar eclipseTotal, annular, partial, hybrid — with obscuration
🌕🌑 Lunar eclipseTotal, partial, penumbral — with geographic location

🔍 Unique feature: clicking any event moves the app to the exact instant of the event with the object locked at screen centre — a direct view of what the calculation described.

🟠 An orange visual frame distinguishes Astro-Calculations mode from manual mode at a glance — it wraps the whole app while the panel is open and disappears when it closes.
about.time_body:
Daily control:

  • ▶️ Start/stop time tracking with ⏸️ pause and instant sync.
  • 🎚️ Continuous speed slider up to ±3 hours/second (forward and backward).
  • ⏪⏩ Time jumps — second, minute, hour, day, month — in both directions.
  • 🕐 Display of Terrestrial Time (TT), local time, 📅 Julian Day (JD), the Julian calendar date and 📐 ΔT.
  • 🔄 A «Now» button for instant return to real time.
about.info_body:
Every clicked object opens a detailed card with independent sections:

  1. 🧭 Altazimuth coordinates — azimuth and altitude at the instant of observation.
  2. 🔵 Equatorial (of date) — after precession.
  3. 🟣 Equatorial (J2000) — the reference frame.
  4. 🟡 Ecliptic — ecliptic longitude and latitude (of date and J2000).
  5. 🌅 Rise/set times — upper transit, sunset and lower transit for the day.
  6. 📊 Object properties — distance, illumination fraction, phase angle, elongation (for bodies); apparent magnitude, Hipparcos number and proper motion (for stars); a full Gaia DR3 section (source ID, G magnitude, both motions, RGB colour); and the full Messier section.
  7. ♈ Signs & mansions — the object's sign in both systems and its lunar mansion with percentage.

Values refresh every second for the selected object and are always computed from the position of the drawn star itself (after proper motion and precession).
about.search_body:
• 🔎 Instant type-ahead search (autocomplete) in Arabic and English.
  • 🎯 Comprehensive coverage — planets, Sun and Moon, Hipparcos stars by name and number, Gaia stars by their IDs, Messier objects, and all 88 constellations.
  • 🧭 Smart navigation — angle normalisation prevents long reverse rotation when jumping across the 360° line.
  • 📍 Lock to Center — keeps any object at the heart of the screen while time flows.
  • 🎯 Centre crosshair — a reference ring showing exactly what the display centre targets (live RA/Dec and Az/Alt) — a perfect tool for verifying proper-motion accuracy.
  • 🚫 Friendly toasts — status messages for every operation (navigation, locking, loading, errors).
about.location_body:
• 🌐 Online city search — Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) with Arabic/English results.
  • ✍️ Full manual entry — latitude, longitude, elevation and time-zone offset.
  • 🕐 Automatic timezone offset via TimeAPI.io with correct support for historical daylight saving (DST) across past and future dates.
  • 🏷️ IANA time-zone name (e.g. Asia/Riyadh) shown with the location.
about.orientation_body:
• 📱 Device Orientation — the device compass and gyroscope steer the celestial dome around you.
  • 🎯 Absolute mode — a true reference bearing, not relative.
  • 🎚️ Adjustable sensitivity from 0.1× to 5.0×.
  • 🔵 Blue visual frame distinguishing simulation mode from manual mode.
about.display_body:
• 🌀 Custom stereographic projection via WebGL shaders — mimicking the feel of the human eye's lens.
  • 🔭 Huge dynamic zoom — FOV from 0.1° (telescopic precision) to 150° (the whole sky).
  • 🏷️ Smart adaptive labels with zoom, and gradual fading of artistic figures when zooming in.
  • 📊 Live FOV and FPS indicators for performance diagnostics.
  • 🌗 Ambient light adjustability + 💡 realistic planet lighting toggle.
  • 🖥️ Fullscreen at one tap.
  • 🎵 Built-in music player.
about.languages_body:
العربية (RTL) · English · Français · Deutsch · Español · Türkçe
Instant switching saved automatically, with translated status messages for every language — and all features (search, settings, calculations, info) work in the chosen language.
about.tech_body:
TechnologyDescription
Three.js r1283D WebGL engine
Astronomy EngineCore astronomical computation engine (VSOP87 + ELP-2000/82)
Custom WebGL shadersStereographic projection and star rendering
Progressive streamingGaia tiles filled in batches ≤7ms — no freezing
Zero allocationReused matrices and vectors to prevent garbage-collection stutter
Smart throttlingUpdate gates (≥0.05 years) instead of recomputing every frame
Cache API + Smart CacheLibraries, Gaia data and Deep Time data stored locally — work resumes instantly after the first download
Pakogzip decompression inside the browser
Single portable fileSelf-contained HTML + local data — ready for APK packaging via WebView
about.refs_body:
Software libraries

  • Three.js — the 3D engine
  • Astronomy Engine — astronomical computations (Don Cross)
  • Pako — gzip decompression

Astronomical data

  • Hipparcos Catalogue — bright-star catalogue (ESA)
  • Gaia DR3 — the billion-star catalogue (ESA) — epoch J2016.0
  • Messier Catalogue — 110 deep-sky objects
  • IAU Constellation Boundaries — the 88 constellation boundaries (1930)
  • JPL Horizons — planetary ephemerides (NASA)

Maps & imagery

  • Solar System Scope — planetary maps up to 8K
  • ESO — Milky Way panorama
  • Wikimedia Commons — additional planetary and lunar maps
  • Stellarium — constellation figure art style

Web services

  • Nominatim — geographic search (OpenStreetMap)
  • TimeAPI.io — time zones and historical DST
  • CDN networks: Cloudflare · jsDelivr — library availability
about.science_body: The app is designed for hobbyists, researchers and students alike. All computations use models adopted by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) and NASA together with the standard motion theories (VSOP87, ELP-2000/82), with validity spanning the full ±9999 years of the original JPL data. Remember that the reference epoch differs between Gaia releases (DR3 at J2016.0) — the app aligns it automatically during propagation.
about.summary_body:
• ✅ IAU 2006 astronomical engine in the of-date frame
  • ✅ 2 million Gaia DR3 stars + live proper motion on the great circle
  • ✅ Bright Hipparcos stars with names and dynamic labelling
  • ✅ 110 Messier objects + the Milky Way panorama (ESO)
  • ✅ 88 IAU constellations with boundaries, names and figure art
  • ✅ Five coordinate grids with adaptive numbering
  • ✅ Three zodiac systems + 4 sidereal references + 28 lunar mansions
  • ✅ 12 categories of astronomical calculations to the second with time-jump-to-event
  • ✅ Deep time ±9999 with compact binary JPL data and Hermitian interpolation
  • ✅ Info panel with four coordinate systems and rise/set/transit times
  • ✅ Instant bilingual search + lock-to-center + centre crosshair
  • ✅ Device-orientation simulation (absolute) with adjustable sensitivity
  • ✅ 6 languages · stereographic projection · 0.1°–150° zoom · music and fullscreen
  • ✅ Engineered performance: ≤7ms batches, zero allocation, throttling, smart cache
  • ✅ Runs in the browser and is APK-packagable — data is local after first download
about.deep_body:
What is Deep Time? An optional system that extends the astronomical engine beyond the safe range of the core library (0–4000 CE), for exploring the sky in the deep past or the far future.

  • 🏛️ Deep past (9999 BCE ← 0) and 🚀 far future (4000 ← 9999 CE) — ~110 MB per range, optional download.
  • ⚡ Compact binary data structure — columnar Float64 layout with gzip and Hermitian interpolation for smooth, accurate planetary motion between samples.
  • 🧠 Smart Cache — downloaded data is stored locally and loads instantly in later sessions without re-downloading.
  • 🛡️ Automatic performance guards — outside the safe range (0–4000) fine time controls hide automatically unless Deep Time is enabled, protecting against costly pointless computations.
  • 🎯 Practical benefits: simulate eclipses, conjunctions and planetary configurations in ancient historical eras, follow the sky's evolution across centuries, while keeping the same level of display accuracy.
